A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Track4Gen. Their main text, equations, six tables, 21 figures, and supplementary sections A–E support reliable comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation and point-tracking evaluations, ablations, qualitative analyses, and a 64-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–6, the user study, and supplementary examples and failure cases.

M1.justification: The SVD backbone, refiner, zero-convolution feedback, gradient routing, joint losses, and tracking procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 expands preprocessing documentation without establishing a redesign of the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training sources, VBench-I2V generation evaluation, TAP-Vid DAVIS and BADJA tracking evaluations, and Kubric/Panning MOVi-E synthetic-data ablation. No evaluated domain or task is added or removed.

E2.justification: The generation comparisons retain pretrained SVD, finetuned SVD, and Track4Gen without its refiner. The tracking comparators in Tables 2–3 and the supplementary DINOv2 comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported training budget, sampling settings, metrics, 355-image generation evaluation, short/full-duration tracking evaluations, and 64-participant study are unchanged. Appendix A.1 supplies additional preprocessing detail without reporting revised experiments.

E4.justification: Both retain the refiner, trainable-module, 2D/3D-convolution, and synthetic-data ablations, along with feature comparisons, adaptation examples, and generation/tracking failure cases. Moving supplementary figures does not add analyses.

E5.justification: Figure 8 already contains user-study error bars in v1 and retains them in v3. Neither version adds an explanation of their calculation, repeated-run counts, seed information, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical entries and rankings, including Track4Gen's FID 26.6 and FVD 724 in Table 1. Figure 8 preserves the preference results and error bars, and the qualitative examples are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 extends the formal filtering specification with a rejection condition combining correspondence disagreement of at least 2 pixels and cycle error of at most 1.5. Equations (1)–(4) remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: jointly learning video generation and point tracking, improving feature consistency, and reducing appearance drift. The revised future-work aspiration is not claimed as an achieved contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the proposed application of tracks to motion guidance and blending with an outlook toward 3D-consistent video generation using automatically annotated videos. Existing result interpretations and limitations concerning motion, occlusions, artifacts, and tracking failures are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly documents an additional correspondence-rejection test and explicitly ties its thresholds to 320×576 inputs. This improves the preprocessing specification without demonstrating that training was changed or repeated; the remaining implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al., 'On unifying video generation and camera pose estimation,' to support its revised outlook, while removing the VBench++ and DreamMotion citations. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Edits include renaming 'Appendix' to 'Supplementary Material,' simplifying cross-references, revising short passages and project-page directions, and expanding funding acknowledgments. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures and tables shift position, Figure 12 moves onto a separate page, and Figure 8 receives cleaner plot styling without changing its data. Some raster figures are resampled; all numbered figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional filtering specification in Appendix A.1 reduces a limited reproducibility gap, although its new intermediate-point notation remains unexplained. The claims, experiments, results, and limitations are otherwise stable, so the overall quality gain is small.
